The top being cropped out can be solved by shifting the background-position down 24px and adjusting the height to compensate:

#header {
 /* your code as it is */
 background-position: 0 24px;
 height: /* your height value + */ 24px;
}

Then, adjust the values after the site goes mobile mode (subverse list goes from 24px to 18px):

\@media (max-width: 950px) {
 #header {
 background-position: 0 18px;
 height: /* your height value + */ 18px;
 }

Delete the backslash \, since Voat's trying to link media to /u/media when it sees the @ symbol.

As for scaling the image with the width of the page, you can do this with the following code:

#header {
 /* your code as it is */
 background-size: 100% 0;
}

However, it will keep its aspect ratio, so the height will also be adjusted. This calls for a dynamic header height, which could get complicated. A better solution (in CSS3) would be to create two background images: one with the sub name and background, and one with the emblem at the right side. If you were to do this, your final code (combined with the code up there) would look like:

#header {
 background-image: url('%EMBLEMURL%'), url('%BANNERURL%');
 background-position: right 24px, left 24px;
 height: /* your current height value + */ 24px;
}
\@media (max-width: 950px) {
 #header {
 background-position: right 18px, left 18px;
 height: /* your current height value + */ 18px;
 }
}

Make sure to delete the \ backslash and that both the emblem and banner are the same height. Let me know if this solution is good enough for you. :-)
